fields.mechanism: Chronic expanding hematomas arising over a decade post primary total hip arthroplasty
fields.intervention: Incorporate a porous coating material with controlled expansion properties that allows for biological integration while accommodating long-term dimensional changes in surrounding bone tissue
fields.expected_effect: Enhanced osseointegration and reduced micromotion at the bone-implant interface, preventing loosening over time
fields.falsification_test: Accelerated fatigue testing of implant-bone interface under cyclic loading with and without the proposed coating, measuring micromotion and interface strength over time
fields.mechanism_source_span: Chronic expanding hematoma (CEH) is an infrequent yet serious complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Mismanagement of this condition can result in severe consequences.

fields.mechanism: Passive fluid drainage through microchannels in the implant interface
fields.intervention: Design hip prosthesis with integrated microchannels that allow for controlled fluid drainage from the bone-implant interface
fields.expected_effect: Prevention of hematoma formation and subsequent chronic inflammation that leads to loosening
fields.falsification_test: Implant testing in simulated physiological conditions with controlled fluid introduction to evaluate drainage efficiency
fields.mechanism_source_span: This comprehensive approach aims to contribute valuable clinical insights into the diagnosis and management of CEH.
